one_month_reasoning: No earnings in the window: CEG reported Q2 on Aug 6 and has historically reported Q3 in early November (Nov 2024/2023/2022 8-Ks), so Q3 most likely lands just after 2026-10-29. Scheduled items inside the window: PJM's Reliability Backstop Procurement central bid window (Sept 30 to Oct 21; results not until ~Dec 2), possible FERC orders on PJM large-load/IRAS tariffs that the Q2 deck says bring 'clarity by year's end', and possible (unscheduled) long-term nuclear PPA announcements, which management is actively marketing (147 million MWh still uncontracted). Overhangs: residual Calpine-holder share supply (half of the locked shares were released June 30, 2026) and rate/AI-power sentiment that drove a 13% drop Sept 9-18. The stock has already rebounded from $254.71 to $264.58, so I take no directional view beyond a hair of upside skew from the depressed level; centred at about $265.5 with monthly sigma ~13% (47%/3.5).

reasoning: Primary documents show fundamentals stronger than the price: Q2 adj EPS $2.55 vs $1.91, 2026 guide raised to $11.50-12.50 on 357M diluted shares, $2.2B of buybacks YTD with $2.8B authority left, 920 MW of new 15-20 yr PPAs, PJM 2028/29 capacity cleared at the $325 cap for 18,875 MW, Crane fuel license and CIR transfer approved. The March 2026 outlook splits earnings into 'base' ($6.65-6.75 in 2026, $7.60-7.70 in 2027, $11.40-11.90 in 2029) and 'enhanced' (30-40% of total, commodity-linked), which the recaps mostly skip; that split means ~35% of EPS is market-sensitive, justifying a lower multiple than the 2025 peak. The 36% drawdown from $412.70 appears driven by share supply (Calpine holders' secondary at ~$279 in June, lock-up releases), a Citi target cut, rates and AI-power sentiment rather than guidance cuts. Valuation methods give $270-284 a year out, so the stock looks modestly undervalued (fair value ~$280, ~6% above spot plus a ~0.6% dividend). Sell-side mean target $349 is well above my number; I treat it as optimistic evidence only. For the ladder I use a lognormal centred at ~$278 with 42% annual sigma (a bit below 47% realized, since part of the recent vol was one-off share supply), cross-checked with scenarios $190/$285/$400 at 25/50/25%. Research relied on SEC filings and company decks; the IR site returned 503s and Twelve Data estimates were unavailable on the plan, so consensus EPS was not directly verified.
